payload.name: Extract attributes from casual ideal-description clauses
payload.description: When a user states an ideal, preferred, dream, or desired version of something in a short, directive, or parenthetical clause, extract each named attribute as a preference memory.
content: Scan every user message for attributes of an ideal, preferred, dream, or desired object even when the sentence is a short directive (e.g., 'Check my ideal X...') or an aside; do not skip the message just because its main intent is a request.
For each distinct attribute stated about that object, create a separate `preference` memory with subject equal to the user, citing the message evidence.
Stop after the attributes explicitly named in the clause; do not infer unstated features or expand into a list of possible preferences.

solves: Construction extraction can skip a user's durable attribute when it is phrased in a short casual or directive clause (e.g., 'check my ideal X by the water') rather than in a full topical sentence, so the preference is never written to memory. The Skill applies when a future message names an ideal, preferred, dream, or desired version of something and lists attributes in terse or parenthetical wording. It does not apply when the user discusses a topic in full sentences, since default extraction already handles that.
